questions.q: In His Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught against seeking revenge. According to Matthew 5:38-39, what did He say a person should do if someone strikes them on the right cheek?
options: Strike them back harder
Report them to the local authorities
Turn the other cheek to them also
Run away immediately
questions.explain: Jesus taught non-retaliation, saying: "You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.' But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Jesus' teaching on forgiveness in Matthew 6:14-15, what is the strict condition for God forgiving our trespasses?
options: We must offer a sin offering at the temple.
We must fast for forty days.
We must forgive others their trespasses.
We must pay all our debts.
questions.explain: Jesus stated clearly: "For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you, but if you do not forgive others their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To cure worrying about earthly needs like food and clothing, what did Jesus instruct His followers to seek first? (Matthew 6:33)
options: Great wealth to secure their future
The kingdom of God and his righteousness
Friendship with the Roman rulers
A steady job in their community
questions.explain: After telling them not to be anxious about their life, Jesus gave the solution: "But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what did the servant who received one talent do with it?
options: He traded it and made one more talent.
He dug a hole in the ground and hid his master's money.
He bought a piece of farmland.
He lost it to robbers on the road.
questions.explain: Out of fear and laziness, the third servant "went and dug in the ground and hid his master's money." The master later condemned him as a wicked and slothful servant.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Talents, what commendation did the master give to the servants who successfully multiplied their talents?
options: "You are now wealthy and free to go."
"Well done, good and faithful servant."
"You have defeated all my enemies."
"You shall rule over the entire Roman Empire."
questions.explain: To both the five-talent and two-talent servants, the master replied: "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31), where was the poor man Lazarus carried by the angels when he died?
options: To the temple in Jerusalem
To Abraham's side
To a grand earthly palace
To the garden of Eden
questions.explain: Luke 16:22 says, "The poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's side. The rich man also died and was buried, and in Hades, being in torment, he lifted up his eyes..."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: While suffering in Hades, what small mercy did the rich man beg Abraham to send Lazarus to do for him?
options: To sing him a hymn of comfort
To dip the end of his finger in water and cool his tongue
To unlock the gates of Hades
To bring him a piece of bread
questions.explain: He called out, "Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the end of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this flame." (Luke 16:24)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), how did the father react when he saw his repentant son returning from a long distance?
options: He ignored him and went inside the house.
He ordered his servants to throw him out.
He felt compassion, ran, embraced him, and kissed him.
He demanded his lost money back before speaking to him.
questions.explain: Luke 15:20 shows God's forgiving love: "But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did the older brother in the Parable of the Prodigal Son react when he heard music and found out a celebration was being thrown for his younger brother?
options: He immediately joined the feast in joy.
He was angry and refused to go in.
He went to town to buy a welcome gift.
He hugged his brother and wept.
questions.explain: The older brother represents the self-righteous religious leaders. "But he was angry and refused to go in. His father came out and entreated him." (Luke 15:28)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: During the miracle of feeding the four thousand (Matthew 15:32-39), which was distinct from the feeding of the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces were collected afterwards?
options: Five
Seven
Ten
Twelve
questions.explain: In the feeding of the 4,000, Jesus started with seven loaves and a few small fish. Afterward, "they took up seven baskets full of the broken pieces left over." (Matthew 15:37)
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When a fierce windstorm struck the Sea of Galilee and waves were breaking into the boat, where was Jesus and what was He doing? (Mark 4:38)
options: He was standing at the front, commanding the wind.
He was in the stern, asleep on a cushion.
He was bailing water out with the disciples.
He was teaching the crowd on the shore.
questions.explain: Despite the raging storm, Mark 4:38 says: "But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they woke him and said to him, 'Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?'"
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Because of the massive crowd gathered around Jesus in Capernaum, how did the friends of the paralyzed man successfully bring him to Jesus? (Mark 2:4)
options: They pushed violently through the front door.
They dug a hole through the roof and let down the bed.
They yelled loudly from the street until Jesus came out.
They sent a written letter to Jesus via a Roman soldier.
questions.explain: When they could not get near him because of the crowd, they removed the roof above him, and when they had made an opening, they let down the bed on which the paralytic lay.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Jesus saw the funeral procession for the widow's son at Nain, He had compassion. What specific action did Jesus take to stop the procession before He commanded the dead man to arise? (Luke 7:14)
options: He shouted with a loud voice to the crowd.
He touched the bier (coffin), and the bearers stood still.
He threw his cloak over the dead body.
He instructed Peter to block the road.
questions.explain: Luke 7:14 details this moment: "Then he came up and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still. And he said, 'Young man, I say to you, arise.'" Touching a burial bier would typically render a Jewish person ritually unclean, but Jesus imparted life instead.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: During the mission of the twelve disciples, Jesus instructed them on what to do if a house or town refused to welcome them or listen to their words. What was this instruction? (Matthew 10:14)
options: To call down fire from heaven to consume the town
To shake off the dust from their feet as they leave
To curse the village leaders publicly
To stay in the town and argue until they listened
questions.explain: Jesus said, "And if anyone will not receive you or listen to your words, shake off the dust from your feet when you leave that house or town." This act symbolized severing responsibility for their rejection of the gospel.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When the seventy disciples returned joyfully from their mission, saying that even demons were subject to them in Jesus' name, how did Jesus describe His spiritual vision of Satan? (Luke 10:18)
options: "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven."
"I saw Satan bound in chains forever."
"I saw Satan running away in fear."
"I saw Satan transformed into an angel of light."
questions.explain: Confirming the disciples' spiritual authority over demonic forces, Jesus replied to them: "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to John 2:11, what was the primary spiritual result of Jesus performing His first miracle—turning water into wine at Cana in Galilee?
options: The master of the feast immediately was baptized.
He manifested His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
The Romans attempted to arrest Him for magic.
The bride and groom offered Him money.
questions.explain: John carefully notes the purpose of this sign: "This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:20-21), what kind of person is represented by the seed sown on rocky ground?
options: One who hears the word and never understands it
One who hears the word with joy, but has no root and falls away when trouble or persecution arises
One who bears fruit a hundredfold
One whose faith is choked by the cares of the world and deceitfulness of riches
questions.explain: Jesus explained: "As for what was sown on rocky ground, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy, yet he has no root in himself... when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, immediately he falls away."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Steward (Matthew 18:23-27), the first servant fell on his knees because he owed the king a massive, unpayable debt of ten thousand talents. How did the king initially respond?
options: He sold the servant into slavery immediately.
Out of pity, he released him and forgave the entire debt.
He ordered the servant's family to work off the debt.
He gave the servant one more month to pay the debt.
questions.explain: Matthew 18:27 displays the king's incredible mercy: "And out of pity for him, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To teach the multitudes about counting the cost of discipleship and evaluating their level of commitment, Jesus used the practical example of a person intending to build what? (Luke 14:28-30)
options: A fishing boat
A new synagogue
A tower
A stone wall
questions.explain: Jesus asked: "For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it?" This illustrated the profound commitment required to follow Him.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Matthew 5:44, as part of the Beatitudes and Sermon on the Mount, Jesus radically commanded His disciples regarding their attitude towards their enemies. He said: "Love your enemies and ________ for those who persecute you."
options: pray
fight
flee
lay traps
questions.explain: Replacing the old standard of hating one's enemy, Jesus elevated the law of love: "But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Beatitudes, Jesus taught: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall ____________." (Matthew 5:8)
options: inherit the earth
see God
obtain mercy
be comforted
questions.explain: According to Matthew 5:8, Jesus promises a profound spiritual reward for internal purity: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to the Sermon on the Mount, what title will be given to the "peacemakers"? (Matthew 5:9)
options: Prophets of God
Priests of the Most High
Sons of God
Kings of the Earth
questions.explain: Matthew 5:9 states, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God." Promoting peace reflects the very character of God.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep (Luke 15:3-7), how does the shepherd react when he loses one sheep out of a hundred?
options: He ignores the lost sheep because he still has ninety-nine others.
He sends his servants to look for it.
He leaves the ninety-nine in the open country and goes after the lost one until he finds it.
He buys a new sheep from the market.
questions.explain: To illustrate God's relentless love for lost sinners, Jesus said the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine in the open country and searches for the one lost sheep until he finds it.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares, the master commands his servants NOT to uproot the weeds immediately. What reason does he give? (Matthew 13:24-30)
options: Because the weeds are actually beneficial for the soil
Because the servants might accidentally uproot the wheat along with the weeds
Because the master wants to sell the weeds at the market
Because the weeds will eventually turn into wheat
questions.explain: The master warned, "No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them. Let both grow together until the harvest." This signifies that the final judgment and separation will occur at the end of the age.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Lost Coin (Luke 15:8-10), what specific actions does the woman take to find her single lost silver coin?
options: She goes to the marketplace to complain to the merchants.
She lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and seeks diligently until she finds it.
She hires a professional investigator.
She ignores it and goes to sleep.
questions.explain: Luke 15:8 explains her thorough effort: "Or what woman, having ten silver coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek diligently until she finds it?"
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: During the miracle of calming the storm (Mark 4:35-41), what exact words did Jesus use to rebuke the wind and the raging waves?
options: "Be gone from my sight!"
"Peace! Be still!"
"Winds, bow down to your creator!"
"Halt in the name of the Lord!"
questions.explain: Jesus awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, "Peace! Be still!" And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Peter attempted to walk on water towards Jesus (Matthew 14:28-31), what caused him to become afraid and begin to sink?
options: He looked back at the disciples in the boat.
A large sea monster appeared beneath him.
He saw the wind and took his focus off Jesus.
His clothes became too heavy with water.
questions.explain: Matthew 14:30 records: "But when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, 'Lord, save me.'" This illustrates the danger of focusing on circumstances rather than maintaining faith in Christ.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins, when the five foolish virgins finally returned with oil and knocked on the door, what did the bridegroom say to them? (Matthew 25:11-12)
options: "You are late, but come in and rejoice."
"Truly, I say to you, I do not know you."
"You must pay a fine to enter the feast."
"Go and sleep outside with the animals."
questions.explain: After the door was shut, the foolish virgins arrived saying, "Lord, lord, open to us." But the bridegroom answered, "Truly, I say to you, I do not know you."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Following the miraculous feeding of the five thousand with five loaves and two fish, how many baskets of broken pieces were left over? (Matthew 14:20)
options: Seven
Ten
Twelve
Fifteen
questions.explain: Matthew 14:20 records the abundance of God's provision: "And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up twelve baskets full of the broken pieces left over."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to the Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:5), what reward is promised to the meek?
options: They shall see God.
They shall inherit the earth.
They shall obtain mercy.
They shall be called sons of God.
questions.explain: Jesus taught, "Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth." This emphasizes that God honors humility and gentleness over worldly aggression.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Jesus called Matthew to be one of His disciples (Matthew 9:9), where was Matthew sitting and what was his occupation?
options: Sitting in a boat, mending fishing nets
Sitting in the temple, studying the law
Sitting at the tax booth, working as a tax collector
Sitting under a fig tree, praying
questions.explain: Matthew 9:9 says: "As Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, 'Follow me.' And he rose and followed him."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Jesus sent out the seventy disciples on their mission (Luke 10:2), He compared the world to a field waiting to be gathered. What did He say about the harvest and the laborers?
options: "The harvest is ruined, for the laborers were lazy."
"The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few."
"The harvest is small, so only a few laborers are needed."
"The harvest will wait until the laborers are ready."
questions.explain: Jesus told them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few. Therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:23), what does the seed sown on good soil represent?
options: One who hears the word but forgets it the next day
One who hears the word, understands it, and bears fruit yielding a hundred, sixty, or thirtyfold
One who preaches the word but does not practice it
One who uses the word of God to gain earthly riches
questions.explain: Jesus explained: "As for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Steward (Matthew 18:28-30), what did the first servant do immediately after the king had mercifully forgiven his massive debt?
options: He went to the temple to offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving.
He found a fellow servant who owed him a small amount and choked him, demanding payment.
He threw a large feast for his friends to celebrate his freedom.
He returned to the king and offered to work for him for free.
questions.explain: Despite being forgiven a debt of ten thousand talents, the servant immediately went out and ruthlessly demanded a hundred denarii from a fellow servant, choking him and throwing him into prison.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25:8-9), what was the response of the wise virgins when the foolish ones asked to share their oil?
options: They generously shared half of their oil.
They scolded the foolish virgins for their laziness.
They told them to go to the dealers and buy for themselves, lest there not be enough for everyone.
They blew out their own lamps so no one would have light.
questions.explain: The wise virgins replied, "Since there will not be enough for us and for you, go rather to the dealers and buy for yourselves." This illustrates that spiritual preparedness cannot be borrowed from another person.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When Jesus sent out the seventy disciples and they returned with joy, He declared that He had given them a specific kind of authority. What was it? (Luke 10:19)
options: Authority to govern the twelve tribes of Israel
Authority to collect taxes on His behalf
Authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy
Authority to call down fire from heaven on unbelievers
questions.explain: Luke 10:19 says: "Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Jesus taught that love is the supreme mark of a Christian disciple. In John 13:35, what did He say would be the result if His followers loved one another?
options: The Roman Empire would finally collapse.
They would never face sickness or poverty.
All people would know that they are His disciples.
They would instantly be transported to heaven.
questions.explain: Jesus said, "By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another."
